day_shape: 90 items: Trump rejects Iran's Qatari-mediated Hormuz-reopening offer while regime channels claim IRGC captured a second US submarine, IDF strikes Hezbollah sites after drone attack and kills Oct 7 abductor Saher Saqr in Nuseirat, Nasrallah second-anniversary messaging heavy, nothing from UK Parliament or OFAC.

threads.label: Hormuz standoff and Trump's rejection
threads.summary: Trump told reporters he rejected Iran's proposal, submitted via Qatari mediators at UNGA, to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for the US ending its blockade of Iranian ports. Foreign Minister Araghchi said Tehran awaited a formal response through mediators; Jerusalem Post and Iran International reported anti-ship missile fire towards the strait and explosions near Qeshm Island.

threads.label: IRGC submarine capture claim
threads.summary: Defa Press and IRIB posted repeated claims that the IRGC Navy captured a second "advanced American terrorist army submarine" in the Strait of Hormuz through an operation combining intelligence and electronic warfare. Iran International noted no independent corroboration; Jerusalem Post separately reported Army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia saying the US could launch a renewed attack on Iran.

threads.label: IDF Gaza strikes and Oct 7 operative killed
threads.summary: The IDF announced Saher Nidal Saqr, who drove the motorcycle used to abduct Noa Argamani and Avinatan Or from the Nova festival, was killed in a strike on Nuseirat, alongside Nukhba commander Ibrahim Fawzi Mohsen and operative Mohammed Kamel Mohsen. The military also released drone footage it said showed a Palestinian operative using a child to move weapons in central Gaza.

threads.label: Hezbollah drone attack and Israeli response
threads.summary: The IDF said Hezbollah launched an explosive drone at Israeli troops in the southern Lebanon buffer zone overnight, causing no injuries, and struck drone-launch and anti-tank missile sites in response. IRIB reported Israel imposed a "complete closure" of the occupied West Bank until 3 October; Jerusalem Post marked two years since Nasrallah's assassination.

threads.label: Sacred Defence Week messaging cycle
threads.summary: Khamenei's office reshared a Sacred Defence Week message crediting "God is greatest" as the fighters' weapon, and Defa Press ran an Iranian Soldier Festival honouring Martyr Mousavi. Army chief General Hatami said the war is "not yet over" and warned of "severe blows"; MP Azizi told Defa Press Iran is moving from a defensive to a "preemptive approach".

threads.label: Iran domestic dissent and governance
threads.summary: Iran International reported families of protesters killed in January's crackdown challenged President Pezeshkian's UN characterisation of the unrest as foreign-driven, saying relatives were unarmed. Jerusalem Post reported Araghchi smiled when questioned about executions; Iran International also covered the eased Korean appliance ban and structural problems in Iran's oil governance.

threads.label: Oct 7 recriminations and Qatar-Gaza diplomacy
threads.summary: Times of Israel reported Netanyahu allegedly told security chiefs before Oct 7 he did not want to authorise Gaza strikes that could jeopardise Saudi normalisation, while the PMO rejected claims Egyptian intel chief Abbas Kamel visited Israel to warn of the attack. Qatar's prime minister accused Netanyahu of being the main impediment to a US-backed Gaza peace plan; Gallant confirmed a pre-attack Sinwar "shake the prisons" message.

events.title_en: "Successor"; heroism beyond the clichés of war
events.summary_en: "Successor"; heroism beyond the clichés of war. In war cinema, heroes are often unwavering and invincible men; but in the film "Successor" by Hossein Emahlaki, his heroism is achieved by overcoming fear and doubt. War cinema has long been trapped in the clichés of flat and lifeless imagery; depicting men who seem carved from stone and where anxiety creates no flaw in the steel of their being. But the film "Successor" directed by Mehdi Shahmohammadi breaks this straw doll and takes us to witness a human who, before fighting on the battlefield, must wrestle with the darkest part of his existence - "forgetting".
